name: Bezuclastinib
status: Investigational. NDAs under FDA review as of 17 Oct 2026
summary: An oral, selective type I tyrosine kinase inhibitor of KIT D816V, the mutation that drives most systemic mastocytosis. It binds the active form of the mutant kinase and shuts off the signal that keeps neoplastic mast cells growing. It is designed to spare closely related kinases and to stay largely out of the brain.

journey.title: Dissolves
journey.text: The dosage form disintegrates and the drug dissolves in the stomach and upper intestine.

journey.title: Absorbed
journey.text: Absorbed across the small-intestine wall into the portal blood. Bioavailability and food effect for bezuclastinib have not been published.

journey.title: First pass through the liver
journey.text: Portal blood passes through the liver before it reaches the general circulation. How much bezuclastinib is lost on this pass has not been published.

journey.title: Distributed, but kept out of the brain
journey.text: Carried in the blood to the tissues. Preclinical studies showed minimal brain penetration, which was a design goal. These are company-sponsored data.

journey.title: Reaches the neoplastic mast cells
journey.text: In systemic mastocytosis, mast cells carrying KIT D816V build up in the bone marrow. D816V was found in 93% of adults with indolent or aggressive SM, and in about a third of them also in CD34+ progenitors and eosinophils.

journey.title: Metabolised
journey.text: Most oral kinase inhibitors are metabolised in the liver, often by CYP3A4. The metabolic pathway of bezuclastinib has not been published.

journey.title: Eliminated
journey.text: Kinase inhibitors and their metabolites usually leave mainly in bile and feces, with a smaller share in urine. Mass-balance data for bezuclastinib have not been published.

mechanism.title: Enters the mast cell
mechanism.text: As a small molecule, bezuclastinib crosses the cell membrane to reach the kinase domain of KIT, which sits on the inside of the membrane.

mechanism.title: Binds the active kinase
mechanism.text: It is a type I inhibitor: it binds the ATP site of KIT D816V while the kinase is in its active conformation. Sunitinib, its partner in GIST, is a type II inhibitor that binds the inactive conformation.

mechanism.title: The always-on signal stops
mechanism.text: D816V switches KIT on without its ligand, stem cell factor (SCF). With the ATP site blocked, the mutant kinase can no longer phosphorylate its substrates, and the growth and survival signal stops.

mechanism.title: Mast-cell burden falls
mechanism.text: Neoplastic mast cells depend on this signal, so they decline. In the APEX trial in advanced SM, 65% of 68 evaluable patients responded by mIWG-MRC criteria.

facts.label: Molecule
facts.value: Oral, selective type I tyrosine kinase inhibitor

facts.label: Primary target
facts.value: KIT D816V (exon 17); preclinical activity against KIT exon 9, 11, 17 and 18 mutations

facts.label: Selectivity
facts.value: Spares closely related kinases; minimal brain penetration in preclinical studies (company data)

facts.label: Why KIT D816V
facts.value: Present in 93% of adults with indolent or aggressive SM (Spanish REMA network, n = 113)

facts.label: GIST combination
facts.value: With sunitinib (type II), covers both KIT conformations. PEAK phase 3: median PFS 16.5 vs 9.2 months, HR 0.50

facts.label: Regulatory status
facts.value: Not approved. FDA target action dates: GIST with sunitinib 30 Nov 2026; nonadvanced SM 30 Dec 2026; advanced SM 29 Jun 2027

needs.why: Not published. Add from the Investigator's Brochure or clinical pharmacology report if you have it.

simplified: KIT is drawn with one extracellular domain and one kinase domain. The real receptor has five immunoglobulin-like domains, a juxtamembrane region and a split kinase domain, and it signals as a dimer.
Downstream KIT signalling (for example PI3K/AKT, STAT5 and RAS/MAPK) is drawn as one growth-and-survival signal.
Systemic mastocytosis also involves mast cells in skin, gut, liver and spleen; the figure follows the bone marrow only.
Steps marked typical describe oral kinase inhibitors in general, because bezuclastinib's human pharmacokinetics have not been published.

sources.text: OncLive. Bezuclastinib demonstrates early promise in advanced systemic mastocytosis (APEX trial coverage; describes bezuclastinib as an oral, potent, selective type I TKI that spares closely related kinases, with minimal brain penetration).

Cogent Biosciences. Preclinical data identifies bezuclastinib as a differentiated KIT inhibitor with unique selectivity to KIT D816V and minimal evidence of brain penetration. Poster, AACR-NCI-EORTC Molecular Targets, October 2021. Company-sponsored.
